hierarchical structures in (nano)composits are created by: surface microfibration of (lign)cellulose fibres; dispersal of microfibrillar cellulose within the matrices of conventional fibre-reinforced composites; and the attachment of nano sized bacterial celluloses onto natural fibres.

the hierarchical structures in the composites can be used to create a strong interface between the matrix and the fibre and to create a strong matrix, thus improving the mechanical performance of the composites.
